changes_from_v2_5: gates.G_prefix: the argmax check covers the target's logits only; the draft's and the confidence logits are judged by the magnitude bound alone. Decided by the author on 2026-11-08 after v2.5's gate job, whose G_prefix failed on that check alone (docs/audit/2026-11-08-M6-闸门诊断.md); v2.5's verdict stands as failed, the gate runs again under this protocol. Everything else is v2.5's

gpu.name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition

main.rule: a clean clone of one commit from a git bundle of the local branch, which stays off the public repository; every line's --commit

order: all lines of one (panel, C, seed) run back to back in one job, by pairs: main.pairs rotated so the i-th seed (0-based) of the dev seeds starts with the (i mod 4)-th pair; the pair in place j (0-based) runs its line with the cache off first when j is even, on first when it is odd, so each pair alternates over the seeds; the second pass of a timing-noise group runs every pair the other way round
kv_budget: C * ceil((max_prompt_len + max_tokens + 7) / 256) target blocks for every line, max_prompt_len over the measured panel and its warm-up panel; a block draft's cache mirrors the target's blocks

warmup.requests: first C of the panel, cycled; for a panel that names a warm-up panel, that panel's first C
warmup.seed: after a warm-up panel of its own, the engine's generator is seeded again with the run's seed, so the measurement draws as a fresh engine would whatever the warm-up drew

timing_noise.runs_in: every main job on its own panel: at the seed and each concurrency the whole group runs a second time right after it; the two runs of a line must be token-identical. N_t is the largest |a/b - 1| of Q_steady over the job's 24 pairs, N_rho the largest |rho_1/rho_2 - 1| over its 9 (C, drafting line), both from valid runs only; without all 24 and all 9, the job's gain and rho verdicts are not given. The 9 share their k0 runs and one seed: an engineering threshold, not independent repeats or a bound

decision.a_beats_b: all paired gains same sign and abs(median) > 2*N_t
decision.report: median (min-max), two decimals; range only if max-min > 0.05. The README's headline, total table and figures are the exception: only the median of the 3 seeds, marked as such; the ranges go in RESULTS
decision.revised: 2026-11-02: the README rule of report decided by the author; the verdicts are unchanged

invalid_if: a step other than a prefill > 3 x the median of its kind
lines of one (C, seed) split across jobs: one job is one directory, protocol and panel, each line at the commit of its tree

verify_schedule.made_by: job A on a G4 runtime at 5bf4cbc: tools/profile_verify_cost.py, then tools/fit_confidence_sts.py; seed 17011's calibration run was invalid (a round 5.15 x its median). The first rerun ran on kernels compiled under TORCH_LOGS=recompiles, which changes the kernels and the outputs, so it is not job A's command and does not count; a clean rerun passed with byte-identical confidences; reviewed by the author before this protocol is frozen

cost_curve.round: one round's phase timings summed, propose through commit_copy, on CUDA events; every row verifies query_len positions through the variable-length path, the confidence copy included; fresh requests of context_len random tokens for every (batch, query_len)
cost_curve.revised: 2026-11-02 from v2.1's external.cost_curve, which timed the verify forward alone: the schedule weighs a whole round

calibration.record: every round, each row's 7 confidence logits and its accepted count; all 8 positions are verified, so 'the first i drafts all accepted' is observed for every i
calibration.method: STS: for i = 1..7 in turn, T_i on the grid minimizing the binary cross-entropy of the survival prod_{j<=i} sigmoid(z_j / T_j) against 'the first i drafts all accepted', T_1..T_{i-1} fixed
report_only: ECE over 10 equal-width bins, per position and pooled, raw and after STS
AUROC of the survival pooled over positions, raw and after STS

replay.rounds: the calibration runs' rounds of C rows
replay.rule: a row with n of its 7 drafts accepted accepts min(n, L - 1) when it verifies L positions; a round's time is the cost table's at its token count, the fixed-length round's at 8 per row
replay.source: 2 x N_t, N_t = 1.26% in the cluster's job 236550, kept until the G4's own is measured

confirm.runs_in: nowhere: M6 runs no confirmation set; the identity job only reads this concurrency

equivalence.reference: repeat 1 of the cluster reproduction, job 236550

G_prefix.prompts: the first per_category entries of each category, with the first entry's private part alone, which must hit nothing, second in the list so the first floor_batch of them mix hits and the miss; then the next two entries of the panel, cut to a length of 0 and of 254 mod 256
G_prefix.donor: the first prompt of the panel's warm-up panel, prefilled and run 2 rounds (k0: decode steps) on a hash table that holds nothing else, run one more round once half the arm's prompts hit, and kept until the arm ends

arms.reference: hashing off: each prompt prefilled alone in one step, then `rounds` of the line's own greedy rounds (k0: decode steps), each the draft's block forward, the target's verification, after_verify and the commit
arms.floor: hashing off: floor_batch prompts at a time, prefilled and run as one batch (a batch short of a graph size pads)
arms.chunked: hashing off: each prompt alone, prefilled in two steps split at its shared tokens (its first block when it has none), the second through the paged path over its own first chunk
arms.hit: hashing on, with the donor: each prompt alone, which must hit exactly its shared tokens
arms.hit_batch: hashing on, with a fresh donor: floor_batch prompts at a time, the private part alone among them

G_prefix.forced: every arm but the reference takes the reference's first token, drafts, verified lengths and commits; a variable-length line verifies (prompt index + round) mod (k + 1) + 1 positions per round in every arm

compared.target: the prefill's last-position logits, then every verification's (k0: decode step's) logits
compared.draft: every round's block-forward logits, and for DSpark the logits it samples from: the Markov bias of the forced previous token added in the model's dtype, as the engine adds it
compared.confidence: a variable-length line's confidence logits every round; no argmax over them

G_prefix.rule: per line and panel and for each compared kind: the largest |arm - reference| of chunked, hit and hit_batch at most floor_multiple x the largest |floor - reference|; for the kinds of argmax_kinds, the argmax agrees wherever the reference's top-2 margin exceeds margin; and every hit as designed, and the writes as gates.G_prefix.writes has them. hit against chunked, which differ only in whose K/V the shared blocks hold, is reported
G_prefix.writes: through every hit arm: the target's and the draft's K/V of the shared blocks bitwise as the donor left them; and after every step of hit_batch, the padding rows' slots in the graphs' slot buffers (verification, draft block, k0's decode) are -1, so they write nothing
G_prefix.scope: a forced trajectory: the same forwards on the same tokens, not the equivalence of the sampling flow; chunked and hit differ in who computed the shared K/V and in what forward shape, not in K/V alone
G_prefix.revised: 2026-11-08, the author's decision after v2.5's gate job: the draft's logits flipped their argmax where the reference's top-2 margin was 0.62-1.25, in the chunked arm, which reuses no K/V, and in the floor arm, which changes only the batch, below the draft's own noise floor of 1.36-1.72; a margin of 0.5 decides nothing there. The draft's logits only change q, which speculative sampling corrects to the target's distribution, so they bear on speed; a wrong reuse of K/V moves them far past the floor, which the magnitude bound judges
G_prefix.verdict_by: outputs/colab/m6-gate-check.py reads the tool's report under this rule; tools/gate_prefix.py, frozen with v2.5, still sets its own passed flag and exit by v2.5's rule, which is not this protocol's verdict

identity.rule: the tree at the job's commit against the reference's tokens, request by request, and the environment against job C's manifest: outputs/colab/m4-preflight.sh, m4-preflight-check.py. dev.lines on D48 at confirm.concurrency, seed 17011, against job C's repeat 1; gates.equivalence's dspark_k7 on K128b under protocol v2.1, against the cluster reproduction's repeat 1
identity.why: with the cache off, the lifted check, the hashing of prefill blocks only, the recorded hits and the warm-up panel must not change a token
identity.also: gates.equivalence's dflash_k7 at its concurrency on K128b under protocol v2.1, against the cluster reproduction's repeat 1
identity.scope: the panels, warm-up and generator of v2.4 with the cache off

document.after: The content of the book is given below.

prefix.system_intro: You are a helpful assistant. Every conversation in this session shares the reference document below; it may be unrelated to the user's request.

dataset.name: nvidia/SPEED-Bench
dataset.throughput_8k: the revision of long_context in v2.4: fa4e669bee2a4393c56aa8ed05a7c667897f9590

prefix.rule:
tools/build_panel_prefix.py: the private parts picked as K128b's are, the first `measured` measured and the rest warm-up only; panel S

is a system turn of exactly P tokens in front of each private part, so its shared part fills P / 256 whole blocks; P = 0 is the private parts alone

main.jobs: one job per panel, in listed order; a job's report and its hits check before the next starts

definitions.window: the steady window of bench-v2: F the prefill steps' time in it, D the time of its steps that decode or verify C rows, I the rest of its time (the gaps between steps and the steps with fewer rows), O the tokens delivered in it by the requests' deliveries, N_pf the requests whose first delivery is on a prefill step in it, N_r its steps of C rows; T the window's time
definitions.G: Q_steady(line_pc) / Q_steady(line) - 1, the same seed and C
definitions.p: F / T, of the run with the cache off
definitions.kappa: kappa_pf = (N_pf / O)(on) / (N_pf / O)(off), kappa_r = (N_r / O)(on) / (N_r / O)(off)
definitions.h_tok: over the N_pf requests of the run with the cache on: the sum of cached_tokens over the sum of prompt_len
definitions.rho_hat_tok: (1 - p_k0 h_tok_off,k0) / (1 - p h_tok_off): the direction note's formula on the runs with the cache off alone, a prediction conditional on them
definitions.rho_hat_0: (1 - p_k0 h_k0) / (1 - p h): the measured prefill saving alone, an accounting
definitions.rho_hat_1: (1 - p_k0 h_k0 - s_k0 d_k0) / (1 - p h - s d): the measured prefill and round, an accounting
definitions.premise: rho_hat_0 and rho_hat_1 are the identity with kappa_pf = kappa_r = 1 and i unchanged; the report lists kappa and f, r, i so the gap between them and rho can be read
definitions.s: D / T, of the run with the cache off
definitions.G identity: 1 + G = 1 / [p kappa_pf (1 - h) + s kappa_r (1 - d) + i(on) / tau(off)], tau = T / O; exact, the same as (f + r + i)(off) / (f + r + i)(on)
definitions.f, r, i: F / O, D / O, I / O
definitions.h_tok_off: shared_tokens x N_pf / (the sum of prompt_len of those N_pf requests), over the run with the cache off: the hit rate the panel's design gives the requests that run prefills inside its window

verdicts.null: on S0 every (line, C, seed) gives the same tokens with the cache on and off, request by request. Otherwise stop_if: the job stops at once, nothing is rerun, and no gain or rho verdict is given
verdicts.hits: with the cache on every measured request of a run has cached_tokens equal to the panel's shared_tokens, with it off every one 0; and the run's prefill_tokens over its measured steps equal its requests' prompt_len - cached_tokens. Otherwise stop_if, as null
verdicts.gain: per (panel, C, line) with all 5 seeds and the job's noise complete: faster when every seed's 1 + G > 1 + 2 * N_t, slower when every seed's 1 + G < 1 - 2 * N_t, else undecided
verdicts.rho: per (panel, C, drafting line) with all 5 seeds and the job's noise complete: decision.a_beats_b on the seeds' rho - 1 with N_rho in place of N_t
verdicts.complete: a (panel, C, line) without all 5 seeds is reported, not judged
verdicts.formula: report only: per (panel, C, drafting line) the seeds' rho - rho_hat_tok, rho - rho_hat_0 and rho - rho_hat_1, median (min-max), and kappa
report_only: f, r, i, p, h, d, h_tok per line, and d of each round phase (propose, verify, ctx_store, the rest)
the mean context of the window's steps of C rows
TTFT p50 and p99 over every request, and over the requests submitted inside both windows of a pair, paired by request, with their counts
tokens per round and the median output length, on and off
the share of requests whose tokens are the same on and off

pilot.report: never: the pilot only sizes the main jobs

stop_if: identity finds a difference: no performance numbers from this tree; find the cause
main.verdicts.null or main.verdicts.hits fails: the job stops at once without a rerun
an invalid run: its whole (panel, C, seed) rerun once, per invalid_if; still invalid: stop

shared_kv.rule: tools/shared_kv_bench.py: the first C prompts of the panel prefilled once with hashing on, after the warm-up panel's first prompt, so every row's shared blocks are one physical copy; then every row's shared blocks copied, target and draft K/V, into blocks of its own. The two layouts are the same state but for the block tables: the same values, tokens, positions and graphs. Each layout, alternating over the repeats, runs the same step at the same position warmup + steps times without committing: k0's decode forward; a drafting line's draft block forward and its verification of k fixed drafts. Reported only: per C and part the median of the timed steps, and d = 1 - shared / private. The draft block forward is not the whole propose: no logits, Markov or sampling

compile_caches: every job archives /content/cache into its OUT when it ends, with the archive's sha256. A new VM restores job D's archive; one that replaces a lost VM restores the newest archive an M6 job left, copied to outputs/colab/ and named through PREP_CACHES and PREP_CACHES_SHA256, and the job records which. identity checks the old panels with the cache off, not the shapes the cache adds; within one job every comparison runs on one VM
